newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai bank chief to balance rates, liquidity.
newsitem.headline: New Thai bank chief to balance rates, liquidity.

text.p: Thai central bank governor designate Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Tuesday he would try his best to balance interest rates and money market liquidity as Thailand adjusted to the baht's new managed float system.

Chaiyawat, picked by the Thai cabinet on Tuesday to replace predecessor Rerngchai Marakanond, told reporters a balanced policy on interest rates and liquidity would help the central bank curb inflation.
Chaiyawat said although he was prepared to work in coordination with the government on national economic policy, the central bank should display a degree of independence to inspire public confidence.
"Although the BOT (Bank of Thailand) is an independent body, it will not work in isolation. Its policy should be implemented within the framework of a national economic policy.
"However, its governor should retain independence in order to win (market) confidence ...future situations and central bank actions will prove if this is the case," he said.

Chaiyawat, a deputy governor before his appointment, called on different economic sectors to have faith in the economy and the central bank. "Confidence is most crucial for smoothing things out, be it confidence in the exchange rate and in financial institutions. People should not resort to panic runs on their deposits," he said.
